1.overview: Solomon gathers Israel’s leaders and the assembly at Gibeon, where he offers sacrifices at the bronze altar and asks God for wisdom and knowledge to govern the people. God grants his request along with riches and honor, and Solomon returns to Jerusalem, where his reign is marked by abundant chariots, horses, silver, gold, and cedar, as well as trade with Egypt, Kue, the Hittites, and Aram.

sections.heading: Solomon and the Assembly at Gibeon

2.overview: Solomon prepares to build the temple and his palace, asking Hiram of Tyre for a skilled craftsman and timber while describing the temple’s purpose and God’s greatness. Hiram agrees to supply the materials and sends Huram-abi, and Solomon counts and assigns the foreign laborers in Israel.

sections.heading: Solomon’s Building Plans and Labor Force
The Laborers Are Counted and Assigned

3.overview: Solomon begins building the LORD’s house in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, at the site prepared by David, in the fourth year of his reign. The chapter describes the temple’s dimensions and gold-covered furnishings, the Most Holy Place with its cherubim and veil, and the two named pillars at the entrance.

sections.heading: Most Holy Place, Cherubim, and Veil

4.overview: Solomon’s temple furnishings include the bronze altar, Sea, basins, lampstands, tables, and courts, with the Sea placed at the southeast corner. Huram completes the bronze work, cast in the Jordan plain in such abundance that its weight cannot be determined, while Solomon provides the gold furnishings and doors for the temple.

5.overview: Solomon completes the temple, places David’s dedicated treasures in its treasuries, and brings the ark and the Tent of Meeting to Jerusalem with Israel’s leaders. The ark is installed in the Most Holy Place, and as the priests and musicians praise the LORD, a cloud fills the temple and the priests cannot minister.

sections.heading: The Ark Brought into the Temple

6.overview: Solomon recounts how the LORD chose Jerusalem and David, fulfilled the promise that David’s son would build the temple, and placed the covenant ark there. Before the assembly, he prays for the LORD to hear from heaven and respond to Israel’s prayers in cases of wrongdoing, defeat, drought, disaster, foreign worship, war, and exile, then asks the LORD to dwell at the temple and remember David.

sections.heading: Petitions for Israel and the Foreigner

7.overview: Fire consumes Solomon’s offerings, the LORD’s glory fills the temple, and Solomon and all Israel dedicate the house with sacrifices and a feast. The LORD appears to Solomon, promises to hear and restore a repentant people, and warns that disobedience will bring Israel’s expulsion and the temple’s ruin.

8.overview: Solomon rebuilds and fortifies cities, captures Hamath-zobah, and assigns labor and military duties across his kingdom. He moves Pharaoh’s daughter from the City of David, orders regular temple worship, completes the temple service arrangements, and sends ships with Hiram to Ophir for gold.

9.overview: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon, tests his wisdom, praises the LORD for establishing him to govern Israel, and exchanges gifts with him. Solomon's wealth, royal splendor, and dominion are described before the account closes with his death and Rehoboam's succession.

sections.heading: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon

10.overview: At Shechem, Jeroboam and the Israelites ask Rehoboam to lighten the burden imposed by Solomon, but Rehoboam follows the young men’s harsh advice, rejecting the elders’ counsel. God’s purpose through Ahijah’s prophecy is fulfilled as Israel rebels against David’s house, Hadoram is stoned, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem, while he retains rule in Judah’s cities.

11.overview: Rehoboam prepares to fight Jeroboam but turns back when Shemaiah delivers the LORD’s command, then fortifies cities in Judah and Benjamin. Priests, Levites, and worshipers move to Judah after Jeroboam establishes rival worship, while Rehoboam’s marriages, sons, and appointments secure his household and kingdom.

12.overview: After Rehoboam and Judah forsake the LORD, Shishak of Egypt invades Judah, and Shemaiah tells the king and leaders that the invasion follows their unfaithfulness. They humble themselves, so Jerusalem is spared destruction but becomes subject to Shishak, who takes the temple and palace treasures; the chapter then records Rehoboam’s reign, his failure to seek the LORD, and his succession by Abijah.

13.overview: Abijah confronts Jeroboam and Israel at Mount Zemaraim, asserting the Davidic covenant and contrasting Judah’s temple worship with Israel’s golden calves and rival priests. Jeroboam’s ambush is routed after Judah cries out and the priests sound their trumpets, and Abijah captures cities before the chapter records the kings’ deaths, Abijah’s family, and the account of his reign.

sections.heading: Abijah and Jeroboam Prepare for War

14.overview: After Abijah’s death, Asa reigns in Judah, removes idolatrous worship, commands the people to seek the LORD, and builds fortified cities during a period of peace. When Zerah the Cushite advances on Mareshah with a large army, Asa appeals to the LORD, who routs the Cushites, and Judah pursues them and takes plunder as far as Gerar before returning to Jerusalem.

15.overview: Azariah tells Asa and Judah and Benjamin that seeking the LORD brings his presence, while forsaking him brings abandonment, and recalls Israel’s distress before urging Asa to act with courage. Asa removes idols, restores the temple altar, gathers the people for a covenant and sacrifices in Jerusalem, removes Maacah as queen mother, and the land has no war until Asa’s thirty-fifth year.

16.overview: When Baasha fortifies Ramah, Asa pays Ben-hadad of Aram to attack Israel, and Judah uses the abandoned building materials to fortify Geba and Mizpah. Hanani rebukes Asa for relying on Aram rather than the LORD; Asa imprisons him and oppresses some of the people, then becomes ill and dies.

17.overview: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah’s defenses, follows the LORD’s commandments, removes high places and Asherah poles, and sends officials, Levites, and priests to teach the Law throughout Judah. The LORD establishes his rule, surrounding kingdoms refrain from war, neighboring peoples bring tribute, and the chapter records Judah’s fortifications and the numbers of Jehoshaphat’s troops.

18.overview: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab and agrees to join the campaign against Ramoth-gilead, but asks first for the word of the LORD. Micaiah predicts Ahab’s defeat despite the prophets’ assurances, and Ahab dies in battle while Jehoshaphat is spared.

19.overview: After Jehoshaphat returns to Jerusalem, Jehu rebukes him for aiding Ahab and acknowledges his efforts to remove idolatry and seek God. Jehoshaphat renews the people’s worship, appoints judges across Judah, and establishes judicial oversight in Jerusalem, charging them to judge faithfully and without partiality.

20.overview: When Moabite, Ammonite, and Meunite forces threaten Judah, Jehoshaphat gathers the people to seek the LORD, and Jahaziel announces that God will deliver them without their fighting. Judah praises the LORD as the enemy forces destroy one another, returns to Jerusalem in peace, and Jehoshaphat’s reign closes with an account of his alliance with Ahaziah and the wreck of their ships.

sections.heading: Judah’s Praise and the Enemy’s Defeat

21.overview: Jehoram succeeds Jehoshaphat in Jerusalem, kills his brothers, follows the ways of Ahab, and faces rebellions by Edom and Libnah, while the LORD preserves David’s house because of his covenant with David. Elijah’s letter announces judgment, and Philistines and Arabs invade Judah before Jehoram suffers a fatal illness and dies without honor.

sections.heading: Jehoram’s Reign and His Brothers’ Deaths

22.overview: Ahaziah succeeds Jehoram as king of Judah and follows the counsel of the house of Ahab, joining Joram of Israel against Hazael before Jehu kills him and his attendants. Athaliah moves to destroy Judah’s royal heirs, but Jehoshabeath hides Joash in the house of God, where he remains while Athaliah rules for six years.

23.overview: Jehoiada organizes the commanders and Levites to crown Joash, the descendant of David, while Athaliah confronts the gathering and is put to death. Jehoiada renews the covenant with the king and people, Baal worship is dismantled and temple service restored, and Joash is seated on the throne as Jerusalem rejoices.

24.overview: Joash does what is right while Jehoiada lives, and together they collect money to repair the LORD’s temple and restore its furnishings. After Jehoiada’s death, Joash turns to idolatry, orders Zechariah’s killing, suffers defeat by Aram, and is assassinated by his servants before Amaziah succeeds him.

25.overview: Amaziah rules Judah with incomplete devotion, executes his father’s murderers according to the Law, dismisses Israelite mercenaries at a prophet’s warning, and defeats Edom. He then worships Edomite gods, rejects prophetic counsel, loses a war to Jehoash of Israel, and is later killed in a conspiracy after fleeing to Lachish.

26.overview: Uzziah succeeds Amaziah as king of Judah and grows powerful through military victories, construction, agriculture, and a well-equipped army while seeking God. In his strength he enters the temple to burn incense, is struck with leprosy, and lives in isolation until his son Jotham governs and succeeds him.

sections.heading: Uzziah Becomes King and Seeks God

27.overview: Jotham succeeds Uzziah as king of Judah and rules in Jerusalem for sixteen years, doing what is right before the LORD while the people continue to act corruptly. He strengthens Jerusalem and Judah, defeats the Ammonites and receives tribute, then dies and is succeeded by his son Ahaz.

28.overview: Ahaz rejects the LORD, adopts idolatrous practices, and suffers defeats by Aram, Israel, Edom, and the Philistines; Israel’s prophet Oded and Ephraimite leaders intervene to secure the return and care of Judah’s captives. Ahaz seeks Assyrian aid without relief, intensifies his worship of other gods, closes and dismantles the temple, and dies without burial in the royal tombs, succeeded by Hezekiah.

sections.heading: Oded Calls for the Captives’ Return
Assyrian Aid Fails to Help Ahaz

29.overview: Hezekiah begins his reign by reopening the temple, calling the priests and Levites to consecrate it, and explaining that Judah’s calamity follows its ancestors’ unfaithfulness to the LORD. After the temple and its furnishings are cleansed, Hezekiah leads sin offerings, burnt offerings, music, and further gifts, and the people rejoice as temple service is restored.

30.overview: Hezekiah invites Israel and Judah to celebrate Passover in Jerusalem in the second month, and the northern couriers meet both mockery and a response from some who come. The assembly celebrates with offerings and joy, Hezekiah intercedes for those who are ceremonially unclean, and the LORD heals the people as the festival is extended and the priests bless them.

sections.heading: Passover Celebrated and the Unclean Healed

31.overview: After the Passover, the Israelites destroy places of worship throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, and Hezekiah reorganizes the priests and Levites and provides for the regular offerings. The people bring abundant contributions and tithes, which Hezekiah’s officials store and distribute among the temple servants, and Hezekiah is commended for acting wholeheartedly in the service of God.

sections.heading: Destruction of Idols and High Places

32.overview: Sennacherib invades Judah, and Hezekiah prepares Jerusalem, encourages its people, and answers Assyrian threats with prayer alongside Isaiah; the LORD delivers the city and Sennacherib returns home in disgrace. Hezekiah recovers from illness, is humbled after pride brings wrath on Judah, prospers, receives Babylonian envoys, and dies as Manasseh succeeds him.

33.overview: Manasseh rules Judah in Jerusalem, profanes the temple and leads the people into idolatry, then is captured by Assyria, humbles himself before God, and returns to Jerusalem to remove idols and restore worship. After Manasseh’s death, Amon reigns wickedly, is killed by his servants, and is succeeded by his son Josiah.

34.overview: Josiah seeks God, removes idolatry throughout Judah and the northern territories, and repairs the temple, where Hilkiah finds the Book of the Law. After Huldah announces coming judgment on the land but peace for Josiah, the king reads the covenant to the people, renews it, and leads a purge of idolatry throughout Israel.

sections.heading: Temple Repairs and the Book of the Law

35.overview: Josiah organizes a Passover in Jerusalem, providing offerings and directing the priests and Levites in the service; the celebration is described as unparalleled since the days of Samuel. Later, Josiah confronts Neco of Egypt at Megiddo, is mortally wounded, and dies in Jerusalem, where Judah mourns him and Jeremiah laments.

36.overview: Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah successively rule Judah as Egypt and Babylon depose or subjugate its kings. After Judah’s leaders reject the LORD’s messengers, the Babylonians destroy Jerusalem and the temple and carry the people into exile, and Cyrus of Persia later proclaims the rebuilding of the temple.

sections.heading: Judah’s Kings Under Egypt and Babylon
